datasets.title: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/vct-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

lineage.description: FAPAR values from VIIRS satellite observations are collected at 10-day intervals. Anomalies are calculated by computing the deviation of each grid cell's FAPAR value from its long-term mean (baseline 2012 to last complete year), producing raster datasets that serve as an empirical indicator of agricultural drought stress on vegetation.

sources.name: Copernicus Vegetation Index (VIIRS)
sources.description: Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) satellite observations of Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) processed by the European Commission Joint Research Centre to generate 10-day composite anomaly grids relative to a 2012-present baseline.
